name: Deathfix
label: Dischord
lede: Fugazi's drummer picked up a guitar and a microphone, found a keyboard player in the back of Bob Mould's Cadillac, and made a D.C. record in love with 1972.

eras.title: In the back of Bob Mould's Cadillac
eras.text: Fugazi had been on indefinite hiatus since 2003, and Brendan Canty was scoring films and running the Burn to Shine series. A long tour in Bob Mould's band put him next to Rich Morel for months, and the two found they loved the same year in rock: 1972.

q: It's like I can scratch this big rock, pop, overblown orchestration itch.
years.h: Bob Mould sidemen Brendan Canty and Rich Morel start Deathfix
years.p: Dischord's history: [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] of [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] and [[Rich Morel|a93f805f-f0f8-4673-b374-2ecc116ea0f2]] of Morel and [[Blowoff|cffa8bae-d631-4cda-a54b-5b8224ec3b1f]] met touring in Bob Mould's band and formed Deathfix in 2009, bonded over glam and prog.
years.xp:
Canty told The Quietus the Mould tour ran about a year and a half, and he and Morel spent months of it riding together in the back of a Cadillac. By the time they got home they knew each other's record collections well enough to start writing.

Back in D.C., Morel came by Canty's warehouse, a big room full of gear Canty had built for soundtrack work, to jam and trade ideas. The touchstones were Bowie, early King Crimson and T. Rex.

years.h: Mark Cisneros and Devin Ocampo join Deathfix
years.p: Two years in, Brendan Canty and Rich Morel's duo becomes a band. [[Mark Cisneros|78448563-93ad-4d49-be7f-95bf5fe60021]] joins on bass and [[Devin Ocampo|10bc183b-b6a8-4769-9e7a-0637d0f8a7a8]], of Medications and [[Faraquet|e866e006-4c80-4753-b53f-1bc5d88ccddd]], on drums, which means Canty stays out front on guitar and vocals.

years.h: Live at Comet Ping Pong, December 9, 2011
yt: Live at Comet Ping Pong, December 9, 2011

eras.title: Seven songs from the warehouse
eras.text: Deathfix's self-titled debut came out on Dischord, the first full record from a Fugazi member's new band in years, and it sounded nothing like Fugazi. By fall 2013 Deathfix had played Coachella, made a video for "Dali's House," and swapped Devin Ocampo for Jerry Busher.

years.p: Deathfix's debut: seven songs recorded at Brendan Canty's warehouse studio in Washington, from "Better Than Bad" to "Transmission." Glam stomp and prog detours, with Canty singing lead.
years.xp:
Rich Morel wrote "Dali's House," which The Quietus described as absurdist namechecks over a shuffling dance groove. Morel's background in dance music and Blowoff, his project with Mould, is all over the record's keyboards.

Canty told The Quietus the perspective on the band had changed 180 degrees since the early days, from a studio hangout into a working group.

years.p: Two months after its debut album, Deathfix is on the 2013 Coachella bill, as We Love DC announced in a Brendan Canty Q&A that month.

years.h: Deathfix releases a video for "Dali's House"
years.p: Hometown Sounds premieres Deathfix's clip for "Dali's House," written by Rich Morel, in early September.

Dischord's history: Devin Ocampo left Deathfix in fall 2013 and was replaced by Jerry Busher of [[French Toast|f9e0402f-c675-46d9-985f-07001bba6480]], who'd played extra drums and percussion with Fugazi. Two old Fugazi hands in one band.

eras.title: Canty's next room
eras.text: Deathfix never announced a breakup, but it has released nothing since the debut. Brendan Canty's next Dischord band, The Messthetics, put him back behind the drums, next to Fugazi bassist Joe Lally.

years.h: Brendan Canty and Joe Lally form [[The Messthetics|62788614-b33c-42c9-9b6e-c9375362b57e]]
years.p: Brendan Canty and [[Joe Lally|62046ffd-7d76-476b-bee5-b281b7575c6c]], Fugazi's rhythm section, team with guitarist Anthony Pirog. Their self-titled debut comes out on Dischord in 2018.
